Section 23(1) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 gives the right to apply to anyone off the roll: 'Any person whose name is not included in the electoral roll of a constituency may apply to the electoral registration officer for the inclusion of his name in that roll.' fix.check: The form's wording supports him on one line, and the conclusion goes further than the documents. The declaration of Form 6 as substituted by S.O. 2802(E) of 17 June 2022 (Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3(ii), No. 2668, para 10, Gazette pages 34 to 36, declaration on page 35, in force 1 August 2022) reads: 'I HEREBY DECLARE that to the best of my knowledge and belief- ... (iii) I am applying for inclusion in Electoral Roll for the first time and my name is not included in any Assembly Constituency/ Parliamentary Constituency. ... (v) I am aware that making the above statement or declaration in relation to this application which is false and which I know or believe to be false or do not believe to be true, is punishable under Section 31 of Representation of the People Act, 1950 (43 of 1950) with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine or with both.' Item (iii) cannot be struck off. Only item (iv) carries '(Strike off, if not applicable)', and the Guidelines appended to the form, para 8 (Gazette page 36), say 'All entries in "DECLARATION" portion should be completed in all respects.' For anyone who was on a roll before, the words 'for the first time' are untrue, and the applicant knows they are. The second half of (iii), that the name is not now on any roll, is true of a deleted elector. Section 31 of the 1950 Act reads: 'If any person makes in connection with— (a) the preparation, revision or correction of an electoral roll, or (b) the inclusion or exclusion of any entry in or from an electoral roll, a statement or declaration in writing which is false and which he either knows or believes to be false or does not believe to be true, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or with both.' One year is the maximum, with a fine as the alternative. The older Form 6 of 2003 carried no such line. Its declaration (iv) read 'my name has not already been included in the electoral roll for this or any other assembly constituency', with an alternative for a name 'included in the electoral roll for ... constituency in ... State in which I was ordinarily resident earlier' (Rules as published by the High Court of Tripura, Form 6 substituted by S.O. 934(E) of 18 August 2003). The 'first time' wording came in 2022. During the SIR, the declarations attached to Form 6 do not ask for it: Annexure D of 24 June 2025 says '(iii) I am applying for inclusion in the Electoral Roll and my name is not included in any other Assembly Constituency/ Parliamentary Constituency', and Annexure IV of 27 October 2025 says '(ii) I am applying for inclusion in the Electoral Roll through Form 6, and my name is not included in any other Assembly Constituency/Parliamentary Constituency' (forms_primary.json). Annexure D was required 'to support the declaration made therein', so it sits beside the Form 6 declaration and does not replace it. Outside the revision the Commission uses the Rules form: Press Note ECI/PN/120/2026 of 26 September 2026, decision iii: 'For non -SIR period, the Forms applicable as per Rules (the Registration of Electors Rules 1960) will be used.' So the special drive under the letter of 1 October 2026 runs on the 2022 form with item (iii) as printed. The Commission's own Manual on Electoral Rolls (March 2023) prints that same form as Annexure 7 (pages 246 to 248) and, at para 14.7.4.1 (page 127), tells a person who 'ceases to be enrolled' to apply again 'through Form-6 (as a new elector)'. It says nothing on how such a person should answer item (iii), and no Commission letter, FAQ or clarification on that point was found. What no document read settles is whether signing item (iii), at an officer's direction and in order to get back on the roll, is an offence. Section 31 needs a statement made knowing it to be false. Whether a court would read that to cover an applicant who signs the Commission's own prescribed form, with every other fact true, is a question for a court. No prosecution under section 31 of anyone re-enrolling through Form 6 was found. 'Have committed criminal offence' is therefore his reading of the law, and no finding supports it. 'Forced' is his word. The letter of 1 October says BLOs 'facilitate enrolment through Form 6' and 'ensure filling up of Form 6'. It contains no compulsion, though for a deleted person it is the only form there is.
